> a big wall display you can tap, like a bigger iphone for your wall. it shows apps, all on one 7 inch touch screen. it runs on an esp32-s3 board and plugs into the wall, so it stays on and you can just glance at it. you can choose on the display itself, either split screen or a single app full screen.

spent 15 hours figuring out the wall display, putting the bom together, and starting the schematic.
i started double sided, then switched to single sided for a bigger screen. it shows apps, and you can pick split screen or one app full screen right on the display.
went with the 7 inch waveshare esp32-s3 board with touch for $38.99, the bigger round ones were too expensive. rest of the bom is a charger, cable, switch cable, and sticky strips. dropped the power bank, and no hanging mount, it sits flat on the wall.
bom without the mount is $56.28 at sale prices before shipping and tax. still gotta confirm the wall, outlet distance, and real checkout totals.
also did the first half of the schematic, just the power chain. wall to charger to cable to switch to board, 5v only. board draws 350ma, charger, cable, and switch are all 3a, so plenty of headroom. second half is still to do.
some images are ai concepts i created for the idea, the rest are product photos or diagrams.

### 2026-11-01: finished the second half of the schematic, display and touch wiring and the flat holder part, and kept building the firmware. the home screen is apps only now, no widgets, and you pick split screen or

**9h**

finished the second half of the schematic, display and touch wiring and the flat holder part, and kept building the firmware. the home screen is apps only now, no widgets, and you pick split screen or a single app full screen right on the display. clock, weather, calendar, timer, tasks, calculator, notes and search all work in the firmware, and maps and mail are built in too, maps from openstreetmap with no key and mail over imap once you connect it yourself. music is display only, no playback, that was the call. camera is dropped completely, this board has no camera connector, and there are no extra boards. nothing needs soldering, everything is plug in.

firmware compiles clean, 1,419,011 bytes, but it has not been tested on the board yet.

### 2026-11-01: ok so after entry 2 i kept going on the ui and honestly this part took way longer than i thought it would.

**8h**

ok so after entry 2 i kept going on the ui and honestly this part took way longer than i thought it would.

first i rebuilt the home screen to actually look like apple homeview, light not dark. big blue clock with just 12 3 6 and 9 and thin hands, and then a dashboard page when you swipe with weather and a small clock and calendar and a greeting. and i finally added real icons to the apps instead of letters, like clock and weather and calendar and timer, all just simple drawn ones, no logos or anything.

then the guestbook app, core memories. you sign by hand first, then it does the chrome animations, then it asks your name and who came with you, then it saves it right on the board with the date and time. you can replay the signature later and favourite it too, thats kind of the whole point, like people actually coming over to sign it.

the rest of the ui got a midnight glass pass as well, dark cards with a thin bright edge and bigger back buttons, but the guestbook stays liquid chrome on its own, thats only for that app.

firmware still compiles clean, 1,521,847 bytes, but it has not been tested on the board yet so im not gonna pretend it has. and i started pushing everything to a new repo, wall-display-ui, lots of small commits, text files only for now, the big firmware file and the images still need manual upload.
